For instance, if the first world-system among the seed-worlds has a retinue equal to the atoms within a buddha-field, the second world-system should likewise have a retinue equal to the atoms within a buddha-field.

This applies from the third and fourth up to the twentieth tier; for every primary buddha-field passed through—downward through the layers—the number of accompanying fields is equal to the atoms within a buddha-field. Thus, proceeding in succession, there are many, many buddha-fields, numbering as many as the atoms within a buddha-field, extending all the way to the twentieth tier, possessing an infinite number.

Regarding the number of worlds in the successive layers, the textual notation is most extensive; however, it merely indicates ten times the number of atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields (*buddhakṣetra-rajas*), as this has not yet reached the number of atoms in *Gaṅgā* river-sand buddha-fields, and is therefore the minimum.
This is because the second layer below already contains a number of worlds equal to the atoms in a buddha-field, and the second layer above doubles that, while the third layer above doubles it again.
Beyond this Ten Floating Banner Buddha-field Diagram,
to the east of the Boundless Exquisite Flower Radiance Fragrant Water Ocean, there is another fragrant water ocean named Stainless Flame Treasury,
from which emerges a great lotus flower named All-Fragrant Mani King Exquisite Adornment World-Germ, called Pervasive Illumination.
Within this world-system of twenty tiers of revolving lands, there dwells this ocean of fragrant water.
To the south of this ocean, there is another ocean of fragrant water named *Inexhaustible Radiant Wheel*; its world-system is named *Buddha Banner Adornment*.
To the right of this ocean, there is another ocean of fragrant water named *Vajra Jewel Flame Light*; its world-system is named *Treasury of Buddha Light Adornment*.
To the right of this ocean, there is a fragrant water ocean named Indranīla-ratna-vyūha;
its world-system is named Illuminating the Ten Directions. To the right of this ocean, there is a fragrant water ocean named Vajra-cakra-vyūha-tala;
its world-system is named Exquisite Intermingled Indra-nets. To the right of this ocean, there is a fragrant water ocean named Lotus...
The world-system seed named Flower Indra-Net is called Universal Manifestation of the Shadows of the Ten Directions;
to the right of this sea, there is a fragrant water sea named Accumulated Treasury of Precious Incense, whose world-system seed is called Adorned with All Majestic Virtues;
to the right of this sea, there is a fragrant water sea named Jewel Adornment, whose world-system seed is called Universally Stainless.
To the right of this ocean, there is a fragrant water ocean named Vajraratnasaṃcaya; its world-system is named Dharmadhātucaryā.
To the right of this ocean, there is a fragrant water ocean named Devapuraratnaprākāra; its world-system is named Jvālāprabha.

(These ten oceans are situated outside the ocean of Exquisite Flower Radiance, surrounding it in succession by circling to the right. Within each of these ten world-systems, twenty tiers of worlds are securely established.)
This Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean is supported by wind-circles as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru;
its most superior wind-circle is named Repository of Supreme Majestic Radiance, which is able to support the Fragrant Water Ocean Adorned with Universal Light Maṇis.
Within this fragrant water ocean is a great lotus flower named Various Radiant Filaments and Incense Banner, the Flower Treasury Adorned.
The Ocean of World-Systems called Adorned dwells therein, surrounded on all four sides by the level, pure, and firm Diamond Ring Mountains.
The oceans, lands, and various trees are each distinct and differentiated.
All the great earth within these Great Cakravāḍa Mountains is composed entirely of diamond, adorned with firmness and indestructible purity.
This great earth is level and without high or low elevations. Within it are oceans of fragrant water, as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Their bottoms are adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels, and their shores are adorned with *maṇi* gems of wondrous fragrance.
Nets made of *vairocana* *maṇi* jewel-kings cover them; the fragrant waters are limpid and transparent, filled with the colors of various jewels.
It is filled with various kinds of precious flowers arranged in swirling patterns upon its surface, while fine sandalwood powder settles as a sediment beneath (and so forth).
Each ocean of fragrant water is encircled by rivers of fragrant water, numbering as many as the atoms in four continents, flowing in a clockwise direction.
Within these oceans of fragrant water, numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, there are ten unspeakable numbers of Buddhas...
World-systems as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field are situated therein, with one at their very center;
the ocean of fragrant water is named Boundless Light of Exquisite Flowers, and the world-system is named Radiant Jewel-Light Illumining the Ten Directions.

Within it dwell twenty tiers of worlds, arranged as previously described in the ocean of fragrant water, Boundless Light of Exquisite Flowers. To the east of that is the [ocean] named Stainless Flame.

Passing through ten fragrant water-oceans, beginning with the Ocean of Fragrant Water named *Gtsang* (Pure), which are as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, one reaches the ocean of fragrant water located nearest to the Cakravāḍa mountain range.
This ocean belongs to the world-system named *Sphaṭikabhūmi* (Crystal Ground), which is called *Nityaprabhāsamukta* (Constantly Emitting Light).
Within it dwell twenty tiers of worlds (though the scripture lists only four names for these tiers). To the south of this *Vimalasāgara* (Stainless Ocean) is...
From the ten seas of incense, such as the Sea of Inexhaustible Radiant Wheels, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields,
one reaches the Fragrant Water Sea near the Cakravāḍa Mountains, named the World-System of Wondrous Tree Flowers,

which gives birth to vast lands in all directions (also consisting of twenty tiers of worlds). To the right of this Sea of Inexhaustible Wheels, there is the Sea of Vajra Jewel Flame Light, and so forth.
From the fragrant oceans numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakable Buddha-fields, there is a fragrant ocean named Boundless Wheel Adornment reaching to the Near-Wheel Mountain;
it is called the World-System of Immeasurable Varieties (also consisting of twenty tiers of worlds).
To the right of this Vajra-Light Ocean, there are ten fragrant oceans beginning with Indranīla-Jewel Adornment, each numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakable [Buddha-fields].

I shall describe the ocean of fragrant waters numbering as many as the atoms within a Buddha-field, reaching as far as the Fragrant Ocean near the Cakravāḍa Mountains, named Tree-Adorned Banner World-System,
which belongs to the world-system called Abiding Imperial Net (also consisting of twenty layers of worlds). To the right of this Blue Imperial Ocean,
there is a sequence of ten fragrant oceans beginning with the Vajra-Circle Adornment, passing through incalculable numbers of fragrant oceans as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, until—

Proceeding further toward the Fragrant Water Ocean near the Cakravāḍa Mountains, there is an ocean named Jambūnada Jewel Treasury, and the world-system therein is named Universal Sound Banner.

Next, there are ten seas of fragrance, beginning with the Sea of Fragrance of the Mass of Vajra-Jewels, numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, which reach as far as the Fragrant Water Sea near the Cakravāḍa Mountains. This world-system is named Indestructible Sea;

From the ten fragrant water-seas, such as the Jewel Crenellated City Sea,

passing through incalculable Buddha-land-microdust numbers of fragrant water-seas until reaching the fragrant water-sea nearest the Cakravāḍa mountains— named the World-System of Accumulated Garlands and Robes,
which manifests wondrous robes (also consisting of twenty layers of worlds)— there are thus ten such fragrant water-seas, numbering as many as the microdusts of incalculable Buddha-lands.

Within the ocean, there are world-systems as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, all resting upon lotus flowers adorned with mani-jewel king banners that manifest the forms of all bodhisattvas. Each is arrayed with boundless adornments without interruption;
each emits jewel-colored light, and each is covered by clouds of light, each uniquely adorned.
Each adorned with distinct kalpa-differences, each with the appearance of distinct Buddhas, each manifesting a distinct ocean of Dharma,
each filled everywhere with distinct sentient beings, each universally entering distinct ten directions,
and each sustained by the spiritual powers of all Buddhas— within each and every such world-system, all worlds rest upon various adornments, abiding in mutual interpenetration.
These form a continuous world-net, established throughout the Lotus Treasury Adorned World-Ocean in all its various distinctions;

(the Lotus Treasury World-Ocean, according to the sutra, consists of one hundred and eleven fragrant oceans, each with a corresponding number of worlds, and the names of these various fragrant oceans are fully detailed in the "Flower Treasury" chapter).

In the *Qīngliáng Shù* (Commentary on the Pure Coolness) regarding the *Huázhàng Yèyīn* (Karmic Causes of the Flower Treasury), it is asked: "While it may be acceptable to describe the Sea of Lotus Fragrance in terms of conventional phenomena, for what reason does the Sea of Buddha-lands (*kṣetra-samudra*) manifest in such a manner?

The answer states: Briefly, there are two reasons. First, with respect to sentient beings: the Tathāgata’s storehouse consciousness (*ālaya-vijñāna*) is itself the Sea of Fragrance, which is also the dharma-nature (*dharmatā*).
The ocean relies upon the essence of non-abiding, which is called the wind-circle (*vāyu-maṇḍala*); this is also the wind of deluded thought (*vikalpa*).

Within this ocean, there are the characteristics of cause and effect—the nature-virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—which are the flowers of the True Cause (*samyak-hetu*). Because they fully encompass all future fruits of both the mundane and supramundane worlds, they are called a "treasury" (*garbha*).
If one takes the Dharma-nature (*dharmatā*) to be the ocean, then the mind itself is the flower; thus, it is also a treasury of containment.

Thus, within the objective aspect (*nimitta-bhāga*) of this storehouse consciousness (*ālaya-vijñāna*), half constitutes the external vessel-world, which is not grasped as a self-nature (the remote objective aspect);

the other half constitutes the internal body, which is grasped as one's own nature and gives rise to sensation and awareness (the immediate objective aspect). For what reason is the Tathāgata-garbha-consciousness thus?
Because such is the nature of phenomena, and because it is projected by karmic actions. Second, regarding all Buddhas: it is maintained by the wind of great vows.

Because the flowers of boundless practices arise from the ocean of compassion, and because the fruits of the two benefits—defiled and pure—overlap without obstruction within the treasury, the characteristics of the manifested lands resemble this;
thus, in the "Appearance" chapter, worlds are frequently used as metaphors for the Buddha’s virtues.
Upon closely examining the meaning of the text, it is because the Buddha’s virtues are like the world, and the world is like them.
The *Zaopo lun* states: "Initially, through the power of great vows, there is the wind-wheel obtained as a result of retribution that sustains all things;
the fragrant ocean obtained as a result of retribution of profound great compassion; and the lotus flower obtained as a result of retribution of boundless great practice.

Furthermore, the lotus flower is the essence of non-reliant wisdom, the palace where great compassion nurtures and gives birth; it is the pavilion where wisdom-illumination observes faculties and responds with compassionate salvation."
The karma of protecting the pure precepts of the *dharmakāya* of equal self-nature results in the attainment of the Cakravāḍa mountains;

the myriad practices that benefit sentient beings result in the blossoming of manifold virtues; and the cultivation of deeds that provide shelter and protection results in the attainment of jewel-trees.
The causes and conditions of such retributive karma are beyond full enumeration. Now, retribution is never obtained in vain; it always has its cause. If...
How does one know the cause and cultivate the fruit? Observing it in this way, it may also be said that they equally shoulder the burden of all beings without weariness;

thus, as a karmic reward, they obtain a precious ground. Because they moisten things according to the directions with great compassion, there are various seas of fragrant water that universally benefit all according to their capacities.
Because they are pure and unstained amidst all worlds, the lotus flowers rise high above the water.

Because all roots of goodness are initiated through various sublime virtues, there is a world-system seed; furthermore, the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) serves as its precious enclosure wall,
the destruction of the heterodox and the establishment of the orthodox serve as its precious banner, it is covered with a precious net representing the interlacing of subtle wisdom,
hung with precious bells signifying the summoning of the sound of the Dharma, and adorned with manifold jewels as a recompense for generosity (*dāna*).
That virtue arises as a response to the merit of diligence; it is augmented by the light that destroys darkness and the fragrant herbs of universal pervasion.
It is a garden for sporting in samādhi, a stream flowing without attachment or obstruction, and the stairway of the Eightfold Path upon which the multitudes may tread.
It is the terrace of the Three Insights upon which the multitudes may ascend—the Dharma-joy.
The joy of meditative concentration puts to shame all other flavors; the necklace of the seven factors of enlightenment makes all other ornaments seem inferior.

The groves of the eightfold liberation are lush and verdant, and the flowers and fruits of the eight liberations are fragrant. One traverses the successive stages of holiness and wanders through every site of enlightenment;
in all these, cause and effect correspond, phenomena and principle complement one another, essence and function are unimpeded, and compassion and wisdom are boundless within the state of mind.
The interpenetration of sacred virtues is immeasurable, and the great deliberations upon divine powers are such that as it is in one *kṣetra*, so it is in ten *kṣetras*.

(This is stated in reference to cases where a single virtue or a single practice exhibits similar causes and effects; however, if one degree encompasses all degrees and one virtue encompasses many virtues, with them mutually interfusing, then this transcends the reach of words and thought.)

Regarding the name "Flower Treasury" (Huazang) for the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean (*Kusumagarbha-vyūha-lokadhātu-samudra*): it is the land of true recompense and non-obstruction where the Tathāgata Vairocana resides.
"Flower" refers to the lotus flower, which takes the form of the Great Jewel Mountain King that supports this world-ocean.
Regarding "the treasury of the calyx-scented banner" (*kukṣi-gandha-ketu-kośa*): the "treasury" (*kośa*) refers to the dwelling place of the lotus seeds;

it signifies that the seeds of all worlds reside within the oceans of fragrant water, just as the seeds of worldly lotuses are contained within their husks. The "fragrant oceans" rest upon a great earth, which resembles the pericarp of a worldly lotus.
As for the "ornaments," these refer to the jewel-ground, the wheel-mountain, the groves of trees, the channels, and the palaces and towers.
The world-oceans, consisting of pavilions, terraces, stairways, railings, jeweled banners, canopies, and precious enclosures; surrounded by flower and fruit gardens;

with jeweled nets suspended in the air and fragrant herbs spread upon the ground; and adorned with rare and precious *maṇi* jewels—these refer to all the twenty-layered worlds within the various world-systems, each being nineteen Buddha-field atoms in height and as vast as the Vajra Mountains in breadth.
Because it is profound, vast, and difficult to fathom, it is metaphorically described as an ocean.
